confidence_note: Robbins built the book on interviews with around fifty financial experts and investors, including Ray Dalio, John Bogle and Carl Icahn (Warren Buffett is referenced but was not a sit-down interviewee in the same way; he is not named here as an interviewee). The reference TR text says the book has 'five steps'; the book is organized around seven simple steps to financial freedom, and the first is making the most important financial decision of your life: to save and invest a portion of every paycheck automatically, i.e. pay yourself first. He also discusses Shlomo Benartzi's 'Save More Tomorrow' approach of committing future raises to savings.
facts: Robbins interviewed about fifty of the world's leading financial experts and investors for the book.
He organizes the book around seven simple steps to financial freedom.
The first step is to make the most important financial decision of your life: commit to saving a percentage of your income and investing it, before spending anything.
He argues the key is to automate it: set up the transfer so it happens before you see the money.
He stresses that most people spend first and save what's left, which usually means saving nothing.
He discusses economist Shlomo Benartzi's 'Save More Tomorrow' idea: commit now to save a portion of future raises, which people find much easier than cutting today's spending.
tension: Almost everyone intends to save. Almost no one has anything left at the end of the month.
opening_idea: Ask fifty top investors for one piece of advice for ordinary people and notice where they start.

lessons.anchor: Step one: the most important financial decision

use_cases.situation: You say you'll save 'what's left' each month.
use_cases.move: Set up an automatic transfer on payday instead.

use_cases.situation: You and your partner argue about money.
use_cases.move: Agree on an automatic savings percentage together first, then budget the rest.

use_cases.situation: Your team manages an employee savings plan.
use_cases.move: Suggest defaulting people into automatic increases with each raise.

pocket_idea: Pay yourself first, automatically, before life decides for you.
